reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis relies on grain boundary strengthening to reduce wear at high temperatures, but for a FeNiCrCoCu HEA, the Cu-rich phase tends to precipitate and coarsen at 600–800 °C, which can dominate wear behavior and make grain size effects secondary; the proposed mechanism is physically possible but has notable gaps regarding phase stability and the role of the substrate.
reasons.testability: The test design is clear and includes a direct comparison of grain size, wear rate, and deformation, with a well-defined falsification criterion, though it lacks specifics on how grain boundary pinning will be achieved and verified in this alloy system.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a relevant mechanism for high-temperature wear of HEA coatings and proposes a practical processing route, but it overlooks the well-known Cu segregation and precipitation issues in FeNiCrCoCu, which limits its direct usefulness to researchers working on this specific alloy.
